threads: Standings after Wk 6: E720, Ligers and FBT 5-1; Viva, Wad, Wet Bandits 4-2; BMB 3-3; DD and Bloodfeast 2-4; Nuts and Scally 1-5; Prestige 0-6.
Streaks: E720 W5, FBT W5, BMB W3; Prestige L6, Scally L5, Nuts L5, DD L3.
Viva: Wk 6 low 432 (penalty); optimal only 438.75. Lost to FBT by 300.75; series now 10-10.
FBT: 732.75 week high; PA 2,991.25, fewest by 450+. Traded for McConkey (12.75 in debut).
E720: second perfect lineup (531/531), FA Tanner McKee 73.75 started. PF 4,158.75 leads league. FAAB $0. Wright ($953) still benched.
Ligers: Cousins started again, 108.25 vs Jones 82.25 bench. $1,000 FAAB untouched.
DD: started Croskey-Merritt and Judkins, both DNP; Dobbins 49.25 bench; opt 577.25 would have won. FAAB $1,000 untouched.
Nuts: Cooper Jr. 102.25 bench, Skattebo started 0.00; opt 608 beats E720. Haven't beaten 720 since 2022.
Scally: started Irving after 165 bench week, 25.25. $103 Dameon Pierce started (53.75).
BMB: 0-3 to 3-3; 1,584.25 over two weeks. $2 Tyrone Tracy 79.25 on bench.
Bloodfeast: traded McConkey to FBT for Adonai Mitchell + $10 + 2027 rookie pick, cut Mitchell 4 days later. $115 Dylan Sampson.
Wet Bandits: $31 Demario Douglas cut before kickoff; $71 Kimani Vidal started (24.75).
Prestige: 0-6, PF 2,881 (443 behind next-worst). Series vs Bloodfeast 7-16.

takes.0005: Full Blown Trash walked into the Game of the Week, a 4-1 vs. 4-1 heavyweight fight, and turned it into a public execution: 732.75 to 432, the week's best score against the week's worst. Tre Tucker (122.75), James Cook (116), Christian McCaffrey (111.75) and Brock Purdy (100) all cleared triple digits, and George Kittle threw in 76.75 because why not. The series with Resistance is now tied 10-10, and Trash has won three straight. They've allowed 2,991.25 points all year, 450 fewer than anybody, which means even their opponents are scared of them. The only blemishes: they traded for Ladd McConkey this week and he started for 12.75, and free-agent pickup Tyler Higbee started for 6.50. Small price. Five straight, 5-1.
takes.0009: Resistance had a week to prove they belonged at the top, and they scored 432. Not a typo. Four thirty-two, the lowest score in the league, and the optimal lineup was 438.75, so there isn't even a bad decision to blame. This roster is just bad on purpose now. Derrick Henry (20.50) and A.J. Brown (20.25) combined for less than Tre Tucker by himself, Aaron Rodgers (92.75) was the only starter worth watching, and the receiver room that scored 3.50 last week celebrated by being only mildly embarrassing. They lost by 300.75, lost the all-time series lead to Trash, and get to send a penalty to the bitcoin pool for the privilege. 4-2, falling fast.
takes.0002: Entertainment 720 is broke, has no waiver money, owns the most expensive bench player in league history, and just set its second perfect lineup of the season anyway. 531 points, 531 optimal. Tyler Shough went from 4.00 to 137, and when the bench was empty, the front office went digging through free agency and came back with Tanner McKee, a backup quarterback, who scored 73.75 in the lineup. Free. Meanwhile Jaylen Wright, the $953 man, remains on the bench, scoring nothing, costing everything. Four straight over Nuts, 12-7 in the series, five straight overall, 5-1, and the most points in the league at 4,158.75. It's not luck anymore. It's annoying.
takes.0006: Nuts lost by 25.25 to the team with no money and left Omar Cooper Jr.'s 102.25 on the bench to do it. Cam Skattebo started. Cam Skattebo scored 0.00. The optimal lineup was 608, which would have beaten 720 by 77, and instead Nuts are 1-5, losers of five straight, and haven't beaten 720 since 2022. Trevor Lawrence scored 152, the second-best quarterback game of the week, and the manager rewarded him by surrounding him with a zero. Ashton Jeanty finally showed up (63) just in time to watch it all burn. At this point the most reliable thing on this roster is the losing streak.
takes.0003: The Ligers have discovered Kirk Cousins, and it's ruining everyone's week. Second straight start, 108.25 points, with Daniel Jones sitting on the bench for 82.25 like a man waiting at the wrong gate. Jonathan Taylor (104.75), Josh Allen (104.25), Kyle Pitts (95, finally allowed to play) and Chuba Hubbard (85.75) buried the Scallywags 672.75–590, the Ligers are 3-0 all-time in this matchup, and the lineup was 2.75 off perfect. They also have $1,000 of FAAB untouched. The defending champs are 5-1, rich, and finally setting lineups like they mean it. Terrible news for the other eleven.
takes.0007: Last week the Scallywags benched Bucky Irving and he scored 165. This week they started him, and he scored 25.25. That is not bad luck. That is a curse, and the manager is the one holding the doll. They also paid $103 on waivers for Dameon Pierce, who gave them 53.75, started Rhamondre Stevenson for 18, and left Tyler Allgeier's 26.50 on the bench. The good news is the optimal lineup (598.5) still loses to the Ligers by 74, so this one wasn't malpractice, just inferiority. 0-3 all-time against the Ligers, five straight losses, 1-5, and every trend line pointing at the floor.
takes.0004: A week after scoring 354.75 with ten healthy bodies, the Wet Bandits spent $103 on waivers, got Kenneth Walker III back (122.25), and won 509.5–486.5. Lowest winning score of the week, and they only got it because the Diamond Dogs started two players who never played a down. Caleb Williams (97.75) and Mike Evans (70.5) helped. Juwan Johnson started and scored 0.00. They paid $31 for Demario Douglas and cut him before kickoff for Brandin Cooks, which is a fun way to set money on fire. The $71 waiver buy, Kimani Vidal, started and scored 24.75. Whatever. A win's a win, the series is 7-6 now, and they're 4-2 with a lot less dignity than their record suggests.
takes.0012: The Diamond Dogs lost by 23 and started two players who never stepped on a field. Jacory Croskey-Merritt: nothing. Quinshon Judkins: nothing. Two empty slots in a 10-man lineup, while J.K. Dobbins scored 49.25 and Chris Godwin 27.75 on the bench. The optimal lineup was 577.25, a 67.75-point win. Bryce Young (113.25), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (100.5) and D'Andre Swift (91.5) did enough to win, and the manager made sure they didn't. And Xavier Hutchinson, the free agent they grabbed this week, started and scored 7.50. Three straight losses, 2-4, $1,000 of FAAB still sitting there untouched like a gym membership.
takes.0011: BMB was 0-3. BMB is now 3-3, and the hottest team in the league isn't close. Malik Nabers (148.75), Drake Maye (130.75) and Bhayshul Tuten (105.5) took Wad of Hell apart 708.25–575.25, ending Wad's four-game streak and pushing BMB's all-time lead in the series to 12-10. They even spent $2 on waivers for Tyrone Tracy and he scored 79.25, though they left him on the bench, so nobody's perfect two weeks in a row. 1,584.25 points in two weeks. Every team that laughed at the 0-3 start should be checking the schedule.
takes.0008: Wad of Hell's four-game win streak ended the way it was always going to end: the first time they ran into a real team. Jordan Love did his job (110). Bijan Robinson, a first-round fantasy pick, started and scored 24.50, which is roughly what you'd expect from a kicker on a bye. Trey McBride added 39.75, and Chigoziem Okonkwo and Jerry Jeudy each scored 51.75 on the bench. Even the optimal lineup loses by 93.75. They're still 4-2 and still second in points, but this team has been winning without ever looking like a winner, and BMB just pointed that out in front of everyone.
takes.0001: Bloodfeast won the Basement Bowl, 659.25–564.25, and for one week they get to look down on someone. Jayden Daniels (120), Isaiah Likely (105.25) and free-agent pickup Jaylin Noel (105.25) led the best score of their season, and the series with Prestige is now 16-7. Keaton Mitchell started for 2.00 with Rico Dowdle's 26.75 on the bench, because some habits don't die in one week. The front office also traded Ladd McConkey to Trash for Adonai Mitchell, $10 and a 2027 rookie pick, then cut Mitchell four days later for Darius Cooper. So they traded McConkey for $10 and a pick. 2-4. Don't get comfortable.
takes.0010: Prestige scored 564.25, their best since Week 1, and lost to Bloodfeast. Bloodfeast. The team that couldn't win a game for a month. Michael Penix Jr. (118.75), Colston Loveland (73.75) and Alvin Kamara (68.25) tried, MarShawn Lloyd started for 5.00, and even the optimal lineup loses by 70. They're 0-6, the only winless team in the league, with 2,881 points, 443 fewer than anyone else. They've lost the series 16-7 and their dignity at a rate that can't be calculated. The Basement Bowl had one winner and one permanent resident, and everybody knows which is which.

dispatch.head: 720, the Ligers and Trash pull away, and the rest of the league starts doing math
dispatch.dek: Entertainment 720, the Ligers and Full Blown Trash all won and sit at 5-1. Resistance, Wad of Hell and the Wet Bandits are 4-2. BMB has won three straight and is 3-3. The Diamond Dogs and Bloodfeast are 2-4, Nuts and the Scallywags are 1-5, and Prestige is 0-6.

dispatch.head: Trash 732.75, Resistance 432: the showdown that wasn't
dispatch.dek: A 4-1 vs. 4-1 game ended in a 300.75-point blowout. Tre Tucker, James Cook, Christian McCaffrey and Brock Purdy all scored at least 100. Resistance's optimal lineup was 438.75, so this wasn't a bad lineup. It was a bad team. The series is tied 10-10, and Trash has won three straight.

dispatch.head: Resistance scores 432, and the bitcoin pool says thank you
dispatch.dek: Derrick Henry (20.50) and A.J. Brown (20.25) combined for 40.75, about a third of Tre Tucker's day. The bench couldn't have saved them. A week ago Resistance was a contender. Now it's in the penalty pool.

dispatch.head: The Diamond Dogs start two ghosts and lose by 23
dispatch.dek: Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Quinshon Judkins were in the lineup and never played. J.K. Dobbins scored 49.25 on the bench. The optimal lineup would have won by 67.75. The Wet Bandits accepted the gift, 509.5–486.5.

dispatch.head: 720 has $0 and another perfect lineup
dispatch.dek: 531 scored, 531 possible. Tyler Shough went from 4 points to 137, and free-agent backup quarterback Tanner McKee scored 73.75 in the lineup. Nuts benched Omar Cooper Jr.'s 102.25, started Cam Skattebo for 0.00, and lost by 25.25. 720 has won four straight in the series.

dispatch.head: BMB went 0-3 to 3-3, and Wad of Hell is the latest to find out
dispatch.dek: Malik Nabers (148.75), Drake Maye (130.75) and Bhayshul Tuten (105.5) ended Wad's four-game streak, 708.25–575.25. BMB has scored 1,584.25 in two weeks. Bijan Robinson started for Wad and scored 24.50.

dispatch.head: The Scallywags finally start Bucky Irving, and he scores 25
dispatch.dek: A week after a 165-point bench game, Irving started and scored 25.25. The Ligers started Kirk Cousins again (108.25), left Daniel Jones (82.25) on the bench, and won 672.75–590. The Ligers are 3-0 all-time in this matchup.

dispatch.head: Bloodfeast escapes, Prestige stays, and McConkey is gone for $10
dispatch.dek: Jayden Daniels (120), Isaiah Likely and Jaylin Noel (105.25 each) won it 659.25–564.25. Prestige is 0-6 and 443 points behind the next-worst offense. Earlier in the week Bloodfeast traded Ladd McConkey to Trash, then cut Adonai Mitchell, the player they got back.

Team of the Week.text: 732.75, the week's top score, in what was supposed to be the game of the year. Five starters over 75 and a 300-point margin over a 4-1 team.

Biggest Bust.text: 432, the week's lowest score, in the week's biggest game. The optimal was 438.75. There's no lineup mistake to blame. It's just the roster.

Luckiest Win.text: 509.5, the lowest winning score of the week, against a team that started two players who never played. Not a win so much as a donation.

0010-0001.head: The Basement Bowl
0010-0001.text: The two lowest-scoring teams in the league: Prestige (0-5, 2,316.75 points) visits Bloodfeast (1-4, 2,665.5). Bloodfeast owns the series 15-7, including a 1,029.75–497.5 beating in 2019 that still sits fourth on the all-time single-game list, but Prestige has won the last two, both by more than 140. Matthew Stafford (180.75) and George Pickens (122.5) are finally playing like a real offense; the problem is a manager who benched 160 points last week. Jayden Daniels (157.25) and Puka Nacua (133) carry Bloodfeast. Whoever starts Kenyon Sadiq loses.

0002-0006.head: 720 goes to Nuts with an empty wallet
0002-0006.text: League-leading 720 (4-1, 3,627.75 points) has won three straight over Nuts and leads the series 11-7; last year's meeting was a 634–415 laugher. Nuts' last win came in 2022, 518.5–511.75, the closest game these two have ever played. Jahmyr Gibbs (192.5) and Christian Watson (157.25) are rolling for 720, but Tyler Shough just scored 4 and CeeDee Lamb 6.75, and with $0.00 of FAAB there's no help coming. Nuts (1-4) need Trevor Lawrence and Sam LaPorta to repeat, and something, anything, from Ashton Jeanty.

0003-0007.head: The champs visit the Scallywags
0003-0007.text: The defending champion Ligers (4-1) are 2-0 against the Scallywags, winning by 61 in 2024 and 232.5 last year. The Scallywags (1-4) have the talent to change that. Their optimal lineup last week was 837.5, and Jared Goff (153.25), C.J. Stroud (112.75) and Bucky Irving (165, on the bench) can keep up with anyone. The question is whether the manager starts Irving over David Montgomery (5.50). On the Ligers' side, the question is whether Kirk Cousins starts two weeks in a row. Josh Allen (154) and Brock Bowers (97.5) don't need a debate.

0004-0012.head: Wet Bandits need ten healthy bodies
0004-0012.text: Week 4's best team just posted the week's lowest score, 354.75, with ten available players and Tyson Bagent at quarterback. Kenneth Walker III and Kyle Monangai, 316 combined in Week 4, weren't in the lineup. The Diamond Dogs (2-3) lead the series 7-5, won last year's game 555.25–498 and hold the biggest margin, 849.75–451.25 in 2017. Their 2020 meeting, 881.75–859.75, is the closest. Mike Evans (115.75) and Davante Adams (88.25) need help. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Ja'Marr Chase are healthy; Sam Darnold and Bo Nix combined for 97.

0009-0005.head: Game of the Week: 4-1 vs. 4-1
0009-0005.text: Resistance and Full Blown Trash are both 4-1 and nearly dead even all-time, Viva up 10-9. Trash has won the last two, and their 2022 game came down to 7.5 points (759.75–752.25). Viva brings Jaylen Warren (165.75), Joe Burrow (132.5) and Aaron Rodgers (121.75), plus a receiver room that started three players for 3.50 last week. Trash has allowed the fewest points in the league and brings Brock Purdy, Dak Prescott, James Cook and Christian McCaffrey. Jameis Winston has outscored both starting QBs from the bench twice. One of these teams falls out of the top tier.

0008-0011.head: The hottest team in the league gets Wad of Hell
0008-0011.text: BMB (2-3) just went perfect for 876, the week's high score, with Drake Maye (211), Parker Washington (143), Jacoby Brissett (137.75) and Malik Nabers (115.75). Wad of Hell (4-1) has won four of five without a monster week, relying on Jordan Love (140.75), Bijan Robinson and Drake London. The series is 11-10 BMB, and BMB won last year's game 539.75–401.75. Wad has the record. BMB has the momentum, two new waiver buys and a front office that suddenly sets perfect lineups. Upset alert.
